items.title: Gucci's better-than-expected Q2 sales send Kering shares higher
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Gucci's Q2 2026 organic sales fell 2 percent, its 12th straight quarterly decline but a clear sequential improvement that beat analyst forecasts, driven mainly by stronger US handbag demand. Kering shares jumped as much as 15 percent on the print. CEO Luca de Meo flagged Q3 as likely 'flattish' and confirmed roughly 100 store closures for the year as part of the turnaround plan, with about 40 percent of 2026 closures concentrated in Asia due to store-network saturation in markets like South Korea, Japan and parts of China.

items.title: Kering sees 'early signs of progress' in Q2, Asia-Pacific ex-Japan flat
items.summary: Asia-focused retail trade outlet's summary of Kering's H1 2026 results: Q2 revenue up 1 percent to roughly US$4.16 billion, H1 revenue down 3 percent, recurring operating margin 12.8 percent. Notes comparable sales in Asia-Pacific excluding Japan were flat, with strong South Korea performance offset by continued Mainland China weakness, while Japan grew 2 percent on tourist spending. Kering closed 84 net stores in H1 2026 toward its 100-store 2026 closure target.

items.title: GlobalData: Kering improves but Gucci still a drag on group performance
items.summary: GlobalData analyst Chloe Tedford-Jones credits new collections under creative director Demna for Gucci's improved but still-negative comparable sales (down 2 percent reported basis). Confirms the same regional split as other outlets -- Asia-Pacific ex-Japan flat, China weak, Korea resilient, Japan up on tourist spend -- and warns geopolitical tension and economic hardship remain downside risks to the recovery despite a positive investor reaction.

items.title: How Luca de Meo's financial overhaul is buying Kering breathing room
items.summary: Analysis piece on Kering's cost-and-inventory overhaul under CEO Luca de Meo, framing the 2026 store-rationalization plan (targeting up to 100-plus net closures, roughly a third tied to Gucci) as evidence the group is stabilizing rather than recovering. Notes that roughly 40 percent of planned 2026 closures fall in the Asian market given store-network saturation, a detail directly relevant to SEA's future retail footprint even though SEA itself was not singled out as a closure target.

items.title: Bernstein: Demna's Gucci runway debut 'more good than bad'
items.summary: WWD trade report on Bernstein analyst Luca Solca's scorecard of Demna's fall 2026 Gucci runway debut, rated 7.6 out of 10, calling reception a mixed but net-positive set of reactions. Piece notes the Milan show was livestreamed to a celebrity-filled Beijing event that briefly boosted online attention across Asia, while a Trinity Asia analyst cautioned that increased 'talkability' has not yet proven it converts into sales, a caveat relevant to Southeast Asian conversion trends as well.

items.title: Thai consumer forum thread asking to authenticate a Gucci item
items.summary: Pantip community thread where a Thai user posts photos asking fellow forum members to verify whether a Gucci item is authentic, with replies discussing telltale signs of counterfeits. Reflects ongoing grassroots consumer wariness about counterfeit prevalence in the Thai secondhand/gray market alongside genuine purchase interest; counted as community-channel volume with mixed/cautionary tone.

items.title: TikTok discovery page shows continued Gucci mini-bag and styling clips trending
items.summary: TikTok's own topic-discovery aggregation page shows a steady stream of user-generated Gucci styling and unboxing short-form videos (mini bags, wallet reviews) continuing to circulate regionally, including Southeast Asian creators. No single post could be isolated with visible public engagement counts at time of collection, so this item is logged as directional SNS-volume evidence only; no reach/engagement figures are asserted.

items.title: PurseForum thread: members compare Gucci's weaker resale value to peers
items.summary: Long-running PurseForum community thread (with recent 2026 replies) where members compare Gucci handbags' comparatively soft secondary-market resale value against Chanel, Hermes and Louis Vuitton, citing style saturation and frequent logo changes as reasons buyers hesitate to pay up secondhand. Critical-angle community sentiment counterweight to brand-side activation coverage; a recurring, not one-off, community view.
